answer: Before filing, the filer must hang the finished work at the pearl market in the karst town for one day, where buyers inspect it and the keeper logs every visitor in the nectar book. The desk checks the book within a day: three real buyers must have seen the work, and one must have signed that it is worth buying. No market day, no visitors, or a book in only the filer's hand means rejection and a 250-coin forfeit, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real market days plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims for work never hung at any market, and all forty fell when the book showed no visitors.
